Paper: Deep learning for computer vision based activity recognition and fall detection of the elderly: a systematic review
Method: Deep Learning (DL) approaches on computer vision data
Metrics / Results: synthesis of recent advancements in DL-based fall detection and HAR for the elderly
Privacy Handling: The review scrutinizes the employed DL models, datasets, and hardware configurations, with particular emphasis on aspects such as privacy preservation
Edge Deployment: The review scrutinizes the employed DL models, datasets, and hardware configurations, with particular emphasis on real-world deployment

Paper: Privacy-Preserved Fall Detection Method with Three-Dimensional Convolutional Neural Network Using Low-Resolution Infrared Array Sensor
Method: A human motion detection system using a low-resolution infrared array sensor was developed to protect the safety and privacy of people who need to be cared for in hospitals and nursing homes. The system uses a three-dimensional convolutional neural network to detect eight kinds of motions, with a focus on fall detection.
Metrics / Results: The proposed method achieved 98.8% accuracy and 94.9% F1-measure in fall detection.
Privacy Handling: The system protects the safety and privacy of people who need to be cared for in hospitals and nursing homes.
Edge Deployment: The system can overcome the limitations of portable devices and optical cameras.
Main Limitation: 1% and 3.6% higher than those of a long short-term memory network

Paper: A Comprehensive Review on Deep Learning Based Fall Detection in Elderly People
Method: Deep learning based fall detection strategies utilizing CNNs, RNNs, and hybrid models.
Input Type: sensor-based and video-based fall detection systems

Paper: SCOUT: An AI-Powered Vision-Based Fall Detection System for Elderly Safety
Method: SCOUT, a home-based, continuous, computer-vision based fall detection system which uses a YOLOv8n deep learning model for the purpose of privacy preserving monitoring at home.
Dataset: A publically available dataset was curated and expanded for training the SCOUT model, specifically for use in detecting falls in older adults.
Metrics / Results: SCOUT achieved the desired performance metrics of detection accuracy $=93$%, precision $=0.94$, recall $=0.945$ and $	ext{F}1$ score $=	ext{0.95}$
Privacy Handling: providing strong user privacy protection by locally computing the object detector results and minimizing transmitted data
Edge Deployment: designed for edge-based deployments, the SCOUT system also has scalable, affordable, and reliable operations in all resource limited environments.

Paper: Hybrid SNN-based Privacy-Preserving Fall Detection using Neuromorphic Sensors
Method: Hybrid framework, the 3D-CNN & SNN (NeuCube) approach, employing Spiking Neural Networks (SNN)
Metrics / Results: Achieved an accuracy of 94.59% with SNN; Improved accuracy to 97.84% using the hybrid approach
Privacy Handling: Employs the Dynamic Vision Sensor (DVS), which captures intensity changes without compromising individuals’ privacy.

Paper: Real-time monitoring of elderly people through computer vision
Deep Hybrid Learning for Acoustic Fall Detection with Parallel Convolutional and Sequential Feature Modeling
Method: The proposed work introduces a hybrid deep learning architecture combining Bidirectional Convolutional neural network (Bi-CNN) with Bidirectional Gated recurrent units (Bi-GRU) also called as Parallel Bi-CNN + Bi-GRU Network (PB-Bi CR-Net).
Metrics / Results: PB-Bi CR-Net significantly outperforms traditional classifiers, providing higher accuracy, robustness to background noise, and better generalization across environments.
Privacy Handling: Fall detection using acoustic signals has gained significant attention due to its non-intrusive, privacy-preserving, and cost-effective nature.
Edge Deployment: This makes the system highly effective for real-time fall event classification, contributing to safer and more reliable healthcare monitoring solutions.
Main Limitation: Traditional machine learning systems such as Logistic Regression Classifier (LRC), Adaptive Boosting Classifier (AdaBoost), Gradient Boosting Classifier (GBC) and Gaussian Naive Bayes Classifier (GNB) rely heavily on handcrafted audio features and simple decision boundaries. Although these models provide baseline performance, they struggle to capture the complex spectral–temporal patterns present in real fall events. Their dependency on manual feature engineering, inability to learn long-range temporal dependencies, and sensitivity to noise limit their reliability in real-world scenarios.

Paper: Human-Centric Edge Intelligence with Gaussian Splatting for Privacy-Aware Elderly Care
Method: A people-focused, privacy-preserving edge monitoring framework using immersive modeling and multimodal sensing. It combines wearable devices, ambient sensors, and vision-based data streams with federated learning.
Metrics / Results: distinct activity signatures across modalities; late-fusion models show superior fall-detection recall than unimodal baselines
Privacy Handling: federated learning to let people train models together without sharing their raw personal data; privacy is further enforced through embedded Gaussian-based visual obfuscation
Main Limitation: issues with class imbalance and noise
